text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- United Nations changes plans on submitting document to Greek and Turkish Cypriot leaders at direct talks in New York next week after Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash threatens not to attend.
- Centre-left United Democrats party will not support lawyer Marios Eliades' bid for presidency until disagreements are cleared up on his manifesto.
- Denktash confirms he will attend New York talks.
- Cyprus Airways report has found two pilots guilty of flight delays during work to rule.
- United Nations will try to ensure prospect of dialogue and lay solid foundations for next rounds of talks.

- Ankara makes significant switch in tactic on Cyprus. Bulent Ecevit is promoting integration of occupied areas (northern Cyprus) with Turkey, which could see Ankara, not Denktash, as Turkish side's official interlocutor on Cyprus issue.
- Turkey is encouraging activities of mafiosos in northern Cyprus which has turned into paradise for money laundering.
- Woman sought for stabbing her husband.
- Hotel industry heading towards crisis as unions decide to take industrial action over alleged violation of collective working agreements by employers.
